name: Seginus
description: A star 27 parsecs away, 3.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71075: radius 3.109 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 32.029 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.067) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71075: effective temperature 7793 +/- 286 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.047)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71075: distance 26.61 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.004), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 27 parsecs away, 3.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 32 times the Sun's luminosity at 7,793 K, so 3.109 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 71075: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Gamma Boötis
quotes.card: Gamma Boötis is a binary star system in the northern constellation of Boötes the herdsman, forming the left shoulder of this asterism.
quotes.introduction: Its name is a Bayer designation that is Latinised from γ Boötis, and abbreviated Gamma Boo or γ Boo.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1487434040320076800 (quality B), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
